articles.title_original: Czechs rally against plan to switch funding of public media
articles.title_zh: Czechs rally against plan to switch funding of public media
facts_zh:
Czechs rally against plan to switch funding of public media
- Published
Thousands of people have gathered in central Prague to protest against the Czech government's plans to scrap the licence fee and use the state budget to fund public media.
Critics say the plans would allow politicians to stifle media freedom.

The coalition government - which consists of the populist ANO party and two right-wing Eurosceptic parties - insists the change will not affect editorial independence, but wants broadcasters to cut costs.

all_titles.en: Czechs rally against plan to switch funding of public media

articles.title_original: Judge blocks Trump closure of 'Trash Island' Washington DC golf course on Sunday
articles.title_zh: Judge blocks Trump closure of 'Trash Island' Washington DC golf course on Sunday
facts_zh:
Judge blocks Trump closure of 'Trash Island' Washington DC golf course on Sunday
- Published
A federal judge has temporarily blocked the US government's closure of an historic golf course and park in Washington DC.
US District Judge Ana Reyes has been overseeing a months-long challenge to the president's plans for East Potomac Golf Links, which he said would be closed from 15 November for extensive renovations.
Reyes has said President Donald Trump cannot close the park nor its golf course, but added that his administration was not required to actively manage either.

all_titles.en: Judge blocks Trump closure of 'Trash Island' Washington DC golf course on Sunday

articles.title_original: Suspected China spy linked to Nvidia's ex-boss left in 2025, Megaspeed says
articles.title_zh: Suspected China spy linked to Nvidia's ex-boss left in 2025, Megaspeed says
facts_zh:
Suspected China spy linked to Nvidia's ex-boss left in 2025, Megaspeed says
- Published
Alice Huang, a suspected China spy who has been linked to Nvidia's former boss Jensen Huang, left her executive role at Megaspeed in August last year, the company says.
Jensen Huang resigned as chief executive of the AI chip-making giant Nvidia after it emerged he had allegedly had affairs with Alice Huang as well as with one of his employees.

Megaspeed is the biggest buyer of Nvidia chips in south-east Asia and the scandal at Nvidia has raised questions about the possibility that high-end AI chips may have ended up in China despite US export restrictions.

all_titles.en: Suspected China spy linked to Nvidia's ex-boss left in 2025, Megaspeed says

articles.title_original: Iran targets US military base in Bahrain with drone attack
articles.title_zh: Iran targets US military base in Bahrain with drone attack
facts_zh:
Iran targets US military base in Bahrain with drone attack
- Published
Iran launched a drone attack against a US military base in Bahrain on Sunday, its second attempt to target the country in three days.
The country's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said it targeted the US air defence radar facility at al-Riffa air base in Bahrain using six drones.
Bahrain's military said its air defence systems intercepted and destroyed the Iranian air attacks "before they could achieve their objectives".

all_titles.en: Iran targets US military base in Bahrain with drone attack

articles.title_original: South Korea's top scorer in tax accountancy exam admits cheating
articles.title_zh: South Korea's top scorer in tax accountancy exam admits cheating
facts_zh:
South Korea's top scorer in tax accountancy exam admits cheating
- Published
A candidate who came first in South Korea's certified tax accountancy exam has admitted cheating by using a miniature camera, mobile phone and AI tools.
Han Won-seok confessed in a video on the YouTube account of his lawyer, Lee Don-Ho, adding that he had confessed to the Seoul Metropolitan Police Agency and offered details on how he cheated.
The 34-year-old scored 397.5 out of 400 points in the first round, getting just one of 160 questions wrong, which initially raised suspicions and sparked online speculation.

all_titles.en: South Korea's top scorer in tax accountancy exam admits cheating

articles.title_original: Three men sentenced to death in Jordan over fatal church mass shooting
articles.title_zh: Three men sentenced to death in Jordan over fatal church mass shooting
facts_zh:
Three men sentenced to death in Jordan over fatal church mass shooting
- Published
A Jordanian court has sentenced three men to death by hanging for carrying out a fatal mass shooting on a church last month.
The attack on 23 October killed nine people and injured 34 others who had been attending a Christian funeral at a Greek Orthodox church in Karak governorate.

Jordan's Armed Forces said in a statement on Sunday that the men had been convicted of committing "terrorist acts", as well as possessing weapons, "promoting the ideas of a terrorist organisation" and "conspiracy to commit terrorist acts".

all_titles.en: Three men sentenced to death in Jordan over fatal church mass shooting

articles.title_original: Pope Leo speaks of community 'suffering' on visit to remote Andes town
articles.title_zh: Pope Leo speaks of community 'suffering' on visit to remote Andes town
facts_zh:
Pope Leo speaks of community 'suffering' on visit to remote Andes town
- Published
Pope Leo XIV has spoken about the "suffering of those who are forced to leave their homeland in search of a better future", which he said had left communities under threat, during a visit to an isolated Andean village in his former diocese.

About 6,000 people live in Santa Cruz de Succhabamba, located in a remote part of the Andes mountains of northern Peru, but the Pope's visit still drew a crowd of about 20,000, according to the Vatican.
At an outdoor Mass, the Pope spoke of "declining birth rates that are emptying villages" and the unequal distribution of the land's resources.

all_titles.en: Pope Leo speaks of community 'suffering' on visit to remote Andes town

articles.title_original: Fifth Canadian soldier dies from injuries caused by large fire at military base
articles.title_zh: Fifth Canadian soldier dies from injuries caused by large fire at military base
facts_zh:
Fifth Canadian soldier dies from injuries caused by large fire at military base
- Published
A fifth Canadian soldier has died from injuries he suffered when a grass fire swept through a military training area last month.

Four people were killed initially and dozens were injured when the fire, which ignited during a live fire training exercise, spread rapidly through Canadian Forces Base Wainwright carried by strong winds on 17 October.
Pte William Douglas Dal Bianco, who had been receiving medical care in Ontario, died on Friday, the Canadian Armed Forces said in a statement.

all_titles.en: Fifth Canadian soldier dies from injuries caused by large fire at military base

articles.title_zh: Israel kills Hamas commander in strike on Gaza camp, officials say
facts_zh:
Israel kills Hamas commander in strike on Gaza camp, officials say
- Published
A senior Hamas figure who helped plan and oversee the 7 October 2023 attack on Israel has been killed in an Israeli airstrike, officials in Israel and Gaza have said.
Samir Abu Younis, the newly appointed commander of the Rafah Brigade, was killed on Saturday in Al-Mawasi in the southern Gaza Strip, according to Hamas's Al-Qassam Brigades military wing.
A local Hamas official confirmed Younis's death.

articles.title_original: Copper wire upgrade behind US flight suspension, transport secretary says
articles.title_zh: Copper wire upgrade behind US flight suspension, transport secretary says
facts_zh:
Copper wire upgrade behind US flight suspension, transport secretary says
- Published
A nationwide US ground stop that caused thousands of flight cancellations and prompted travel chaos was caused by a technical issue following a copper wire upgrade, the transport secretary has said.

Sean Duffy told a news conference that the government was trying to find out whether the problem that led to air traffic controllers suspending take-offs for four hours on Friday had been caused by "incompetence" on the part of the company doing the upgrades or faulty equipment.
Though the ground stop was lifted on Friday evening, it had a knock-on effect on air travel on Saturday as airlines attempted to clear a backlog of flights.

all_titles.en: Copper wire upgrade behind US flight suspension, transport secretary says
